What is photogrammetry?

La photogrammetry is a technique that consists of reconstructing 3D models from 2D images taken from different angles. It is based on the triangulation to determine the exact position of each point on an object, generating a point cloud, then a textured 3D mesh. This method is used both in industry and in preservation of heritage, theAR/VR, or even the quality control.

🧠 From 2D to 3D: how images become models

‍

‍

Once images are accurately captured, the photogrammetry process follows four main steps:

1. Triangulation

The software analyzes the similarities between images and calculates the 3D position of each point.

2. Point cloud

A set of spatial points recreates the volumes of the object.

3. Meshing

The cloud is transformed into continuous surface (mesh) representing the exact shape.

4. Texturization

The captured images are projected onto the surface to restore the textures And the colours real.

faqs.question: Why invest in 3D now?
faqs.answer: With the rise of generative artificial intelligence, 3D is becoming a strategic lever for differentiating oneself. It makes it possible to create immersive, interactive and personalized experiences based on controlled visual data. Unlike images generated exclusively by AI from text prompts, 3D models derived from photogrammetry are based on real objects. This guarantees optimal visual fidelity and essential consistency, especially in the fields of e-commerce, quality control or augmented reality applications.

faqs.question: How does AI enhance the value of 3D models?
faqs.answer: Artificial intelligence acts as an amplifier of the visual potential of 3D. Once a model is generated, it can be animated, stylized, or scaled up using AI-based tools. These tools make it possible to transform a model into a product video, interactive content or advertising asset in a few clicks. AI also makes it possible to automatically adapt the rendering according to the distribution channels: web, mobile, print, etc. The combination of photogrammetry and AI thus constitutes a modern, flexible and highly efficient production flow.

faqs.question: What tools transform a point cloud into usable visuals?
faqs.answer: Once the point cloud is generated from multi-angle images, specialized software can be used to create a textured 3D model. Some of the best known are RealityCapture, Agisoft Metashape or Meshroom for reconstruction. Blender, Cinema4D or 3ds Max then provide rendering and animation. To produce still images or 3D packshots, engines like KeyShot, OctaneRender or V-Ray are used. On the video side, solutions like After Effects with Element 3D or Blender allow you to create product animations. Finally, some tools like ShotFlow make it possible to integrate this content into automated marketing production workflows.

faqs.question: Why is photogrammetry complementary to artificial intelligence?
faqs.answer: Photogrammetry provides a solid and reliable basis. It produces visual data from real objects, with geometric precision that is difficult to obtain with AI alone. Artificial intelligence then intervenes to automate processing tasks, enrich content, generate combinations and streamline distribution. AI does not replace photogrammetry; it values it. The result is visual content that is both faithful, customizable and adapted to multi-channel uses.

Combined with photogrammetry software and AI tools, Orbitvu becomes an essential link in industrializing the creation of 3D models from real products.
